_comment: HUMAN-NEEDS RUBRIC for the proactive surface audit (DR-0086). This is the inspectable, extensible spec the deterministic audit runs against EVERY served surface (surfaces.js registry) every NAS-loop cycle. It encodes the human-obvious questions Darrell should never have to ask (endless-scroll list, static tiles, unreachable admin, dead-end 'coming soon') as machine checks, so they are caught before he sees them. Darrell is the GOVERNOR, not the QA. Add a rubric item here and the engine (scripts/lib/surface-audit-core.mjs) enforces it; the audit CLI (scripts/surface-audit.mjs) files each finding to the in-app Concerns & Solutions board and the event reel. DETERMINISTIC + $0 + NO LLM: every check is a regex over real source or a cross-check of the real registry against the real render. A model is reserved ONLY for judgment items (kind:'judgment', not run by the deterministic loop). Proven-to-catch per DR-0076: each item ships with a synthetic-fixture test that shows it CATCHES the break before it can go green.

dimensions.dynamic-not-static: Numbers and lists are derived from real data, not painted. A hardcoded tile on a trust surface is worse than none.
dimensions.intuitive-ux: Consumer-familiar: newest-first where expected, period/sort/filter controls, paginated (no endless scroll), grouped, mobile-tidy.
dimensions.reachability: Every built surface is reachable IN-APP. No admin/console-only dead surfaces.
dimensions.freshness: Latest data shows as latest; pipelines populated. No '0 of N' where it should be full; the served build is the merged build.
dimensions.no-dead-ends: No white-screens, no 'coming soon' gate without a named, dated reason (active-by-default; DR-0075 requires why + re-review date).
dimensions.works-when-used: The surface actually works when used like a human would — no fake green.
dimensions.self-explaining: Every data-driven surface carries a LIGHT inline what/where/how, and its DEEP Help entry is kept CURRENT (surface-help.js + help-freshness). A stale Help entry is clutter creeping back onto the surface. Enforced by scripts/help-freshness.mjs (filed here as findings; the CI gate is help-freshness.test.js).

items.label: Placeholder / coming-soon content on a shipped surface
items.fix: Replace the placeholder with a real-data surface, OR gate it with a named, dated reason (DR-0075: why + re-review date). A visible surface must invite a real next action, not a dead end.

items.label: TODO / FIXME left in a shipped surface
items.fix: Resolve the TODO/FIXME or convert it to a tracked concern with a re-review date (DR-0075). Unresolved markers on a user-facing surface are silent stalls.

items.label: Hardcoded currency figure rendered on a surface (suspected static tile)
items.fix: HEURISTIC — verify by hand. A dollar figure baked into JSX text (not {derived}) is a painted number. Trace it to a real row/sum (e.g. lib/account-balances.js) or remove it. A static financial tile erodes trust (Reality-Trace P15).

items.label: Hardcoded percentage rendered on a surface (suspected static progress/stat)
items.fix: HEURISTIC — verify by hand. A percent baked into JSX progress copy (a '60% complete' bar) that is not {derived} is a painted number and cannot flag its own miss (the 2026-06-13 Build-board lesson). Derive it from real state or remove it. (Layout widths like style={{width:'100%'}} are intentionally NOT matched — that is CSS, not a data tile.)

items.label: Long-list surface without pagination or windowing (endless-scroll risk)
items.fix: This surface can render a long list. Add pagination or windowing (like BooksTransactions' pageSize=25 + page controls) so it never becomes an endless scroll — consumer-familiar and mobile-tidy. If the list is provably bounded-small, add the surface to this check's excludeSurfaces with a note.

items.label: Registered top-level surface with no render branch in the shell (unreachable in-app)
items.fix: The surface is in the surfaces.js registry but the shell has no `view === '<id>'` render branch, so a user can never reach it in-app (the 'admin not reachable' class). Wire a nav entry + render branch, or remove the dead registration.

items.label: A month in the ledger is anomalously thin or missing vs its neighbors (data-completeness)
items._comment: From the 2026-07-01 incident: a sync 1,000-row cap silently truncated the ledger so April rendered 2 of 296 transactions. This item registers the deterministic check monthCoverage() in app/src/lib/transaction-analysis.js — over the span first..last month (gaps filled as 0 so a MISSING month is caught), flag any month whose count is < 20% of the median populated month. Run over the live ledger (a data pass over data.transactions), not source; the deterministic source loop skips this kind like it skips 'judgment'. Proven-to-catch by month-coverage.test.js.
items.fix: A near-empty or missing month means rows are not reaching the surface (sync cap, parser gap, or un-ingested source file). Trace ingested-vs-source per month and backfill so every month in the span is complete; the ledger is the money loop's ground truth.

liveProbes._comment: OPTIONAL online freshness checks (deterministic HTTP; run only with --online). Each probe GETs a URL and asserts an expectation. Ships EMPTY so the audit is inert online until a real endpoint is configured (no invented endpoints — Verification Doctrine). Add e.g. {"id":"served-app","dimension":"freshness","severity":"critical","url":"https://poetech.us/","expectStatusMax":399,"fix":"..."} or a harvest-count probe {"id":"harvest-transcripts","expectBodyMatches":"\"count\":[1-9]","fix":"transcripts pipeline at 0 — check wf/import"}.
